content: Metatheria is a classification within the class Mammalia. It was first introduced by Thomas Henry Huxley in 1880. This group is almost synonymous with the earlier taxon Marsupialia, which was established by Illiger in 1811. However, Metatheria is slightly broader in scope because it also includes the closest fossil relatives of marsupial mammals. The earliest known representatives of Metatheria date back to the uppermost Lower Cretaceous period in North America. The closest living relatives of metatherians are the Eutheria, another group also defined by Huxley in 1880. Both Metatheria and Eutheria are traditionally classified as infraclasses within the subclass Theria, as described by Parker and Haswell in 1897. The subclass Theria encompasses all living mammals except for monotremes. The term Metatheria is derived from the Greek words metaand theria, which translate to changed beasts.
